title: Identity, Tenant, Roles, and Permissions
goal: Make identity, tenant isolation, role governance, session state, and permission checks explicit enterprise gates before sensitive workflows become live.
userImpact: Founders and operators get a governed path toward multi-user enterprise use without enabling auth execution yet.
commandCenterImpact: P135.1 preserves current Command Center UX. Future P135.4 will own scoped Auth Governance UX changes.
safetyImpact: P135.1 blocks login, sessions, tenant mutation, role mutation, permission grants, permission enforcement, auth providers, DB/runtime writes, provider/model calls, agent dispatch, project mutation, deploy, release, export, package, network calls, and spend.
costImpact: No provider spend. Local metadata/checker validation only.

subphases.title: Contract / Policy / Safety Boundary
subphases.narrowGoal: Start P135 with an implementation-grade identity/tenant/RBAC contract, seven-subphase split, safety boundary, checker, docs/status handoff, and planned-only P135.2 handoff.
subphases.dataShape: Adds P135 contract, plan, checker, roadmap/status records, and validation report only. No auth schema, tenant store, role store, permission engine, session adapter, auth provider, DB adapter, dashboard source, Playwright source, or live execution is added.
subphases.commandCenterUx: Preserve existing Command Center UX. P135.1 does not change dashboard source, labels, controls, routes, or theme behavior. P135.4 owns future scoped Auth Governance UX changes.
safetyRules: Do not enable login, signup, logout, session creation, session refresh, password flows, OAuth flows, SSO flows, or auth provider calls in P135.1.
Do not mutate tenants, users, roles, permissions, memberships, sessions, or identity records in P135.1.
Do not enforce permissions, grant permissions, revoke permissions, assign roles, or evaluate access decisions as live authority in P135.1.
Do not write DB/runtime state, create auth schemas, run migrations, connect auth providers, dispatch agents, mutate projects, deploy, release, export, package, use network calls, or spend.
Do not expose raw private IDs, auth provider payloads, raw JSON, raw logs, raw policy dumps, mutation controls, provider controls, deploy controls, package controls, or spend controls in primary UX.
